A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ME-POIs research and contain 14 readable pages, including Appendix A.1–A.3. Full-text comparison and rendered-page inspection support comparison of the text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on Los Angeles and Houston mobility data, including baseline comparisons, loss ablations, and analyses of anchor and sparse POIs in Tables 1–5 and Figures 3–4.

after.justification: v2 retains the original experimental results in Tables 1–5 and Figures 3–4, including baseline comparisons and ablation analyses.

M1.justification: Sections 2–3 retain the same visit encoder, contrastive POI alignment, multi-scale distribution transfer, anchor supervision, text alignment, and downstream prediction procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Los Angeles and Houston datasets and five tasks, with permanent closure evaluated only in Los Angeles. Appendix A.1.2 changes 'directional interest' to 'visit intent' without changing the existing task definition or labels.

E2.justification: Tables 1–4 retain the same seven text embedding configurations and eleven mobility baselines. Figure 4 also retains the same OpenAI-large, Gemini, CTLE, and TrajGPT comparators.

E3.justification: The preprocessing, task metrics, frozen-embedding evaluation, 60/20/20 split, model configurations, and training budgets remain unchanged in Section 4.1 and Appendix A.1.

E4.justification: The loss-component ablation in Table 5, distribution-transfer analysis in Figure 3, and comparison across anchor and sparse POIs in Figure 4 are unchanged.

E5.justification: Tables 1–5 continue to report averages over five runs, and Figure 3 retains identical error bars. No seed, uncertainty-estimation, or significance-reporting practices are added or revised.

E6.justification: Tables 1–5 and Figures 3–4 retain identical scores, rankings, and findings. No experimental result entries are added, removed, or corrected.

T1.justification: The problem formulation, Equations 1–18, and computational-complexity discussion in Appendix A.3 are unchanged. No mathematical assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about capturing POI identity and function, transferring visitation patterns to sparse POIs, and improving map-enrichment predictions.

C2.justification: Interpretations of mobility/text complementarity and sparsity transfer remain unchanged, as do qualifications about the visit-intent proxy, Houston closure labels, and future applications.

D1.justification: The appendices retain the same preprocessing instructions, baseline model identifiers, hyperparameters, optimizers, hardware, and prompt example. Data-source and access disclosures are unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are unchanged. Geo2Vec changes from an AAAI 2026 'to appear' entry to its 2025 arXiv preprint, while Poly2Vec gains PMLR and page details; these are bibliographic metadata updates for existing references.

P1.justification: Appendix A.1.2 replaces two occurrences of 'directional interest' with 'visit intent,' matching terminology already used elsewhere. Dates and bibliographic wording are updated; section organization and other prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Bibliographic and terminology edits produce small line-wrapping and vertical-spacing changes on the reference pages and first appendix page, including slight repositioning around Table 6. All figures and tables retain their content and design.

improvement.justification: Standardizing 'visit intent' in Appendix A.1.2 removes a naming inconsistency with the task definition and result tables. The expanded Poly2Vec reference also improves bibliographic specificity. These are limited clarity improvements; the methods, empirical support, and reproducibility information remain unchanged.
